title: Socket, HTTPS and object isolation boundary
summary: WebSocket consumes already-authorised streams. Client access receives SocketProvider streams; server wss receives an HTTPS-owned plaintext duplex wrapper. WebSocket never acquires native sockets or TLS objects and preserves peer/address/message objects instead of flattening authority.
invariants: SocketProvider / SocketSelector remains carrier-acquisition authority for direct client access.
WebSocketAccess obtains client streams through SocketProvider~streamSender[At]() and SocketStreamAdapter.
For wss server access, ooRexx HTTPS remains owner of accepted TCP, TLS/OpenSSL, HTTP parsing, bounded admission and cleanup.
WebSocketServerAccess receives only the parsed Upgrade object, plaintext duplex wrapper, peer/address projection and already-read post-header bytes.
No raw Socket, BIO, SSL, SSL_CTX or Foreign Runtime object crosses the HTTPS handoff.
WebSocketConnection, WebSocketServerConnection and WebSocketMessage remain full ooRexx objects.
Underlying peer/SocketAddress identity remains authoritative and must not be reduced to host:port text.
Applications must not grow WebSocket-specific TCP/TLS ownership, routing, credential or identity paths.
